19. (cos(90° + θ) + 1)(sin(360° - θ) - 1) =

A. -cos² θ
B. -sin² θ
C. cos² θ
D. sin² θ
reasoning: First, we use trigonometric identities to simplify the terms: cos(90° + θ) = -sin θ and sin(360° - θ) = -sin θ. Substituting these into the original expression gives (-sin θ + 1)(-sin θ - 1). This is a difference of squares in the form (a + b)(a - b) where a = -sin θ and b = 1, resulting in (-sin θ)² - 1² = sin² θ - 1. Since sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, then sin² θ - 1 = -cos² θ. Therefore, the answer is A.
